conversation.title: Is Technology Good for Society?
conversation.goal: Give a clear opinion on technology, support it with a reason and example, and disagree politely.

turns.text: Hi, I'm Priya from debate club. I think phones make our society more connected. Do you agree with me?

I partly agree with you. Phones make people more connected, for example I can talk to my grandmother abroad every day. However, I think they can also make us less connected in real life, because many people are interested about their screens more than about the person next to them. Was my sentence correct?
No, 'interested about' should be 'interested in', but your view is clear. Why do you think people look at their screens so much?

I think people look at their screens so much because social media is designed to keep them interested. For example, when I get a notification, I feel I must check it immediately. Also, many people are used to fill every quiet moment with their phone, so they are afraid of being bored. Is that sentence correct?
Notifications are a fair point, but I still think real conversation matters more. How do you feel about filling your spare minutes with your phone?

Honestly, I think it depends on the situation. Although I sometimes use my phone in spare minutes, for example to read news, I'd rather talk to a friend if somebody is with me. Do you think it is wrong to check the phone while waiting for a bus? Was my answer correct?
Yes, 'I'd rather talk to a friend if somebody is with me' is correct. Do you ever feel distracted when your phone buzzes during a chat?

judge.voice: I liked that it caught 'used to fill' and told me the rule straight away. It quoted my exact words and the partner answered my 'was that correct?' questions. Help appeared without leaving the conversation. But the help was babyish for me: 'Said more simply', then a gloss of 'connected', and no real B2 starter. When I got the 'try it again' question I repeated my slip, and the recap still called it 'Tried again', which is not honest. The 'spare minutes' rule felt overstated, and 'read news' went unflagged, so I would re-check things myself. I'd use it for opinion questions, but I wouldn't yet trust it to replace my tutor.
